text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos met Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic and leaders of opposition coalition. He says stable, peaceloving and progressive Yugoslavia is in the interest of Greece.
- Pancevo oil refinery processed more than two million tonnes of oil in 1996. It was owed the dinar equivalent of $110 million at the end of last year.
- Zastava car factory ownership transformation model will be completed by end of January, says director of economics institute Danko Djunic.
- Situation on foreign exchange market will be stabilised, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Svetozar Krstic.
- "We are to adopt curriculum plans as soon as the Nis electoral commission defines local election results," says rector of Nis university Branimir Djordjevic.
NASA BORBA

- Several state banks will put on sale for 28 million German marks at the official exchange rate according to a plan of the federal government and the central bank aimed at taking dinars off the streets.
- Ruling party plans to only partially recognise local election results of November 17, source tells paper.
- Vesna Pesic, leader of Civic Alliance of Serbia, one of opposition coalition Zajedno partners, visiting Paris Monday and Tuesday at invitation of the Socialist Party of France.

- Piero Fassino of Italian Foreign Ministry to visit Belgrade Monday where he is to meet representatives of the government, opposition coalition Zajedno, the student protest and other organisations. Zajedno leaders due to visit Italy on January 17.
- Protests over annulment of November 17 local election results continue in Belgrade, Nis, Kragujevac. Protesters plan to celebrate Orthodox New Year on the streets Monday night.
- Representatives of farmers' trade union to meet Serbian Agriculture Minister Nedeljko Sipovac to discuss their demands for payment of autumn crops.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Consumer basket of basic foods and drinks for a four-member family stood at 1,397 dinars in December, which is four percent down on November, says statistics office.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- There are no obstacles to establishment of air links with Bosnia while talks are still under way with Croatia, says Branko Bilbija, director of federal flight control office.
- International community has good intentions to reduce tensions in Brcko area, says Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic in talks with U.S. envoy John Kornblum.
- Nis electoral commission verifies 32 mandates for coalition Zajedno, 28 for the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia and decides to repeat elections in nine electoral units.
